en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa-kanda
4. The Training Rule on the Reinstatement of One Who Has Been Suspended At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī was one who caused quarrels, who caused strife, who caused disputes, who caused contention, and who caused legal issues within the Saṅgha.
The nun Thullanandā protested while that formal act was being performed against her.
Now at that time, the nun Thullanandā had gone to a village on some business.
Then the Saṅgha of nuns—
Thinking, “The bhikkhunī Thullanandā has departed,” she suspended the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī for not seeing her offense.
When the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had finished that business in the village and returned again to Sāvatthī,
the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī did not prepare a seat for the incoming bhikkhunī Thullanandā.
She did not set out water for washing the feet, a footstool, or a foot-washing stone; she did not go out to meet her to receive her bowl and robe;
nor did she offer her water for drinking.
Then the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī:

“Noble lady, why is it that when I was coming, you neither prepared a seat, nor set out water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a foot-wiping cloth; nor did you go out to meet me to receive my bowl and robe, nor did you offer me water?
“It is so, noble lady, because I am one who has no protector.
“But why, noble lady, are you one who has no protector?”
“Venerable lady, these bhikkhunīs have suspended me for not seeing an offense, saying: ‘This woman is helpless and unknown; she has no one to stand up for her.
Thus spoke the bhikkhunī Thullanandā.
“These women are foolish and incompetent; they do not know what is a formal act, nor the defect in a formal act, nor the failure of a formal act, nor the success of a formal act.
We, however, know what is a formal act, the defect in a formal act, the failure of a formal act, and the success of a formal act.

We shall have a formal act performed that has not been performed, or we shall cause a formal act that has been performed to be annulled. Having thus very quickly convened the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, she reinstated the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī.

Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as above] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying: “How can the noble lady Thullanandā restore a bhikkhunī who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without having asked permission from the Saṅgha that performed the act and without knowing the consent of the group? … [The Buddha said: “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā restored a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha? … [as above] … “It is true, Blessed One. … [The Buddha rebuked her as before. … “Indeed, bhikkhus, this is a wrong course for the bhikkhunī Thullanandā … [as above] … Therefore, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā is to be dealt with according to the rule. … [The Buddha laid down the rule: “Whatever bhikkhunī should restore a bhikkhunī who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without having asked permission from the Saṅgha that performed the act and without knowing the consent of the group, that bhikkhunī is to be dealt with according to the rule. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is insane, one who is deranged, one who is afflicted by pain, one who is a eunuch, and one who is a hermaphrodite. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not insane, one who is not deranged, one who is not afflicted by pain, one who is not a eunuch, and one who is not a hermaphrodite. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who has committed a pārājika offense, one who has committed a saṅghādisesa offense, one who has committed a pācittiya offense, one who has committed a pāṭidesanīya offense, and one who has committed a dukkaṭa offense. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who has committed a dubbhāsita offense, one who has committed an offense of wrong speech, one who has committed an offense of wrong thought, one who has committed an offense of wrong action, and one who has committed an offense of wrong view. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a schismatic, one who supports a schism, one who sides with a schismatic, one who is a follower of a schismatic, and one who is a partisan of a schismatic. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a schismatic, one who does not support a schism, one who does not side with a schismatic, one who is not a follower of a schismatic, and one who is not a partisan of a schismatic. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of Devadatta, one who is a follower of Kokālika, one who is a follower of Khaṇḍadeviyā-putta, one who is a follower of Samuddadatta, and one who is a follower of Sāgata. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of Devadatta, one who is not a follower of Kokālika, one who is not a follower of Khaṇḍadeviyā-putta, one who is not a follower of Samuddadatta, and one who is not a follower of Sāgata. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of Ajita, one who is a follower of Pakudha Kaccāyana, one who is a follower of Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, one who is a follower of Makkhali Gosāla, and one who is a follower of Pūraṇa Kassapa. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of Ajita, one who is not a follower of Pakudha Kaccāyana, one who is not a follower of Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, one who is not a follower of Makkhali Gosāla, and one who is not a follower of Pūraṇa Kassapa. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of the Ājīvakas, one who is a follower of the Ābhassaras, one who is a follower of the Subhakiṇhas, one who is a follower of the Vehapphalas, and one who is a follower of the Aviha. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of the Ājīvakas, one who is not a follower of the Ābhassaras, one who is not a follower of the Subhakiṇhas, one who is not a follower of the Vehapphalas, and one who is not a follower of the Aviha. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of the Andhakas, one who is a follower of the Uttarāpathakas, one who is a follower of the Mahāsanghikas, one who is a follower of the Gokulikas, and one who is a follower of the Ekavyohārikas. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of the Andhakas, one who is not a follower of the Uttarāpathakas, one who is not a follower of the Mahāsanghikas, one who is not a follower of the Gokulikas, and one who is not a follower of the Ekavyohārikas. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of the Vajjiputtakas, one who is a follower of the Sabbatthivādins, one who is a follower of the Mahimsāsakas, one who is a follower of the Dharmaguptakas, and one who is a follower of the Tāmraśātīyas. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of the Vajjiputtakas, one who is not a follower of the Sabbatthivādins, one who is not a follower of the Mahimsāsakas, one who is not a follower of the Dharmaguptakas, and one who is not a follower of the Tāmraśātīyas. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are to be restored. … [The Buddha said: “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of persons who are not to be restored: one who is a follower of the Mahāsaṅghikas, one who is a follower of the Caitikas, one who is a follower of the Sarvāstivādins, one who is a follower of the Haimavatas, and one who is a follower of the Vātsīputrīyas. These, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of persons who are not to be restored. There are these five kinds of persons who are to be restored: one who is not a follower of the Mahāsa

“Without having obtained the permission of the Teacher’s instruction according to the Dhamma and the Vinaya, and without knowing the consent of the Saṅgha that performs the act, he reinstates [the monk] without the approval of the group.
“It is true, Blessed One,” [he replied].
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... [as before]...

"How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, without having obtained the consent of the Saṅgha that performed the act and without having informed the Saṅgha that had performed the act according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, reintegrate a bhikkhunī who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... [as before]..."
And furthermore, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:
“Whichever bhikkhunī, however, reinstates a bhikkhunī who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction,
without having obtained the consent of the Saṅgha that performed the act and without the approval of the group— this bhikkhunī also commits an offense entailing immediate confession.”
"Having committed an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which is a formal act involving exclusion.
"But whichever" means whichever such [person]... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"A united Saṅgha" means:
One who shares the same residence and stands within the same boundary.
"Suspended" means suspended for not seeing an offense, or for not making amends for it, or for not relinquishing it.
"According to the Dhamma and according to the Vinaya" means by whichever Dhamma and by whichever Vinaya.
"By the Teacher's instruction" means...
By the teaching of the Jina means by the teaching of the Buddha.
"Without having obtained leave from the Sangha of those who perform the formal act" means without having requested permission from the Sangha that performs the legal procedure (*kamma*).
"Without knowing the consent of the community" means not having ascertained the consent of the community. If,
thinking "I shall reintegrate him," one searches for a community or demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).

For the motion (*ñatti*), there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*); for two proclamations (*kammavācā*), there are offenses of serious transgression (*thullaccaya*); at the conclusion of the proclamation, there is an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*).
The phrase "this too" is said with reference to the preceding [offenses].
"An offense involving immediate transgression" means that one commits it simultaneously with the misconduct regarding the matter, without having been formally admonished.
"Leading to expulsion" means...
He is expelled from the Saṅgha.
It is a Saṅghādisesa...
[as before] ...therefore it is called a Saṅghādisesa.
If it is a legitimate legal procedure (*dhammakamma*) and one perceives it as such, yet one carries it out [to its conclusion], there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If it is a legitimate legal procedure but one is uncertain of it, yet one carries it out, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If it is a legitimate legal procedure but one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure (*adhammakamma*), yet one carries it out, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if he restores [the person] after having obtained the consent of the Sangha that performs the formal act,
or if he restores [him] after having ascertained the desire of the assembly.
She reintegrates one who is still engaged in the formal process;
she reintegrates her before a Saṅgha that does not constitute a quorum for performing the act;
she is insane.
"By one who is a first offender":
thus ends the fourth Saṅghādisesa training rule.
